## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Jhānasodhanajātaka* (Ja 134) is a short birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection. Its narrative frame is set at Jetavana and concerns Sāriputta, the "Captain of the Faith" (*Dhammasenāpati*), who delivered an expanded exposition at the city gate of Saṅkassa in response to a terse query posed by the Buddha [Fausböll 1877; Horner, Vinaya Pitaka vol 1]. The canonical verse begins with the opening words *Ye saññino* [Fausböll 1877]. In the accompanying story of the past (*atītavatthu*) set during the reign of Brahmadatta in Bārāṇasī, the Bodhisatta—who is identified with Mahābrahmā—recounts a past life involving his senior pupil (*jeṭṭhantevāsika*), identified as Sāriputta [Fausböll 1877].

  The text was edited by V. Fausböll in the first volume of *The Jātaka together with its Commentary* (1877) and indexed in the final volume (1897) [Fausböll 1877; Fausböll 1897].
